prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a new 2008 portrait illustration for an established dark Jackie Leven tribute website series.
Image 1 is the ORIGINAL 2008 photograph: primary authority for identity, age, facial proportions, substantial build, curly hair, dark short-sleeved open-neck shirt, thoughtful upward glance, acoustic guitar and relaxed playing gesture.
Image 2 is an approved 2006 illustration of the SAME man: supporting series reference for the dark neutral palette and treatment of guitar, face and hands. Do not copy its downward gaze or pose.
Image 3 is the approved drawing STYLE reference: match its graphic reduction, large calm grey ink planes and rough broken brushwork. Do not use its younger face or hairstyle.

Create a new vertical 4:5 waist-up composition of Jackie Leven circa 2008 with an acoustic guitar across his lap. Preserve his recognizable full face, broad cheeks, substantial chin and neck, exact characteristic eyes, nose and mouth, mature age, medium-length tousled curly hair and stocky torso. Do not slim, beautify, rejuvenate or genericize him. Keep the head tilted slightly up and his thoughtful eyes looking up toward the viewer's left, as in the original photograph. Reconstruct the little area covered by the microphone naturally, with a relaxed closed mouth consistent with his features. No microphone, stand, cables, sheet music, stage equipment or lettering.

Make room for the guitar and BOTH hands. Head and shoulders occupy the upper part, with the recognizable acoustic guitar body and its sound hole in the lower half. The right forearm rests across the upper curve of the guitar and the right hand is relaxed near the strings and sound hole. His left hand rests naturally on the neck, fingers curling around the fingerboard. Gently angle the neck toward the upper right to fit the portrait frame; keep the entire fretting hand inside the image. The guitar body should be recognizably complete and both arm-to-hand connections anatomically coherent. No additional fingers, extra limbs, broken joints or distorted instrument. Recompose for this upright format instead of copying the landscape concert snapshot.

Render everything as visibly hand-drawn, reduced dry-brush ink. Three or four main neutral tonal groups, broad simple facial planes, precise sparse strokes for eyes and lips, grouped curls rather than individual hairs. Simplify hands to clear anatomical masses with selective lines, not detailed skin. Reduce guitar to its large curved silhouette, sound hole, bridge, a few straight string marks and suggested frets; no photoreal wood grain, decorative rosette, brands or tiny hardware. The guitar is muted grey and charcoal, never bright wood-coloured. Shirt and background remain largely dark negative space. Energetic irregular strokes describe the sleeve, arm, shoulder and guitar edges. Keep the graphic economy of image 3: no airbrushed photographic modelling, dense stippled skin, repeating microtexture, glossy paint, vector shapes or digital mosaic.

Palette and mood: subdued watermark-like presence, strictly neutral charcoal and grey on almost black anthracite #0d0f12. No sepia, brown, ochre, cream, red stage light or cyan tint. Muted mid-grey highlights rather than white glare; facial planes should be no brighter than in image 2. Natural positive lighting, with dark pupils and nostrils. Near-featureless dark background with a few quiet brush gestures. Let hair tips, clothing, lower torso and outer guitar edges dissolve softly into the surrounding darkness without obscuring the instrument or hands. One standalone portrait, vertical 4:5, no border, text, logo or signature.
